name: Translate-train / translate-test / back-translation (NLLB-200, HiTZ mt-hitz (Itzuli-lineage), OPUS-MT, MADLAD-400)
links: NLLB-200: facebook/nllb-200-distilled-600M, facebook/nllb-200-distilled-1.3B, facebook/nllb-200-3.3B (NLLB Team 2022, arXiv:2207.04672). HiTZ MT (Marian, EN/ES/GL/CA <-> EU): HiTZ/mt-hitz-en-eu, HiTZ/mt-hitz-eu-en, HiTZ/mt-hitz-es-eu, HiTZ/mt-hitz-eu-es (collection huggingface.co/collections/HiTZ/machine-translation); Itzuli is the Basque Government online MT service. OPUS-MT: Helsinki-NLP/opus-mt-en-es, opus-mt-es-en, opus-mt-en-eu, opus-mt-eu-en (Tiedemann & Thottingal 2020) [uncertain on exact eu repo names]. MADLAD-400: google/madlad400-3b-mt, -7b-mt, -10b-mt (Kudugunta et al. 2023, arXiv:2309.04662). Evidence papers: Artetxe et al. 2023 'Revisiting Machine Translation for Cross-lingual Classification' (EMNLP, arXiv:2305.14240); Heredia et al. 2024 'XNLIeu' (NAACL, arXiv:2404.06996, github.com/hitz-zentroa/xnli-eu, includes MNLI machine-translated to Basque); Artetxe et al. 2020 'Translation artifacts in cross-lingual transfer learning' (EMNLP).
year: NLLB-200 2022; OPUS-MT 2020 onward; MADLAD-400 2023; HiTZ mt-hitz models 2023-2024 [uncertain]; methodology papers 2020-2024
license_access: Open-weight, local inference. NLLB-200 weights CC-BY-NC-4.0 (non-commercial; fine for shared-task research). HiTZ mt-hitz models Apache-2.0. OPUS-MT CC-BY-4.0. MADLAD-400 MT models Apache-2.0. Itzuli web/API is a public-administration service with its own terms (API use may require registration) [uncertain].
track_coverage: T2 ES and T3 EU: translate-test (ES/EU -> EN, then English model) and back-translation paraphrase augmentation. T4 mixed: translate-test by normalising both sides to EN (or to one language). T1 EN: only round-trip (EN -> ES/EU -> EN) paraphrase augmentation. Translate-train of the task data itself is largely moot because the organizers already ship human-verified ES/EU/mixed training files; translate-train remains useful for auxiliary data (MNLI/SNLI/iSTS/PhrasIS -> ES/EU).
basque_quality: Basque is supported by all four systems. HiTZ model card (eu->en BLEU): Flores-200 devtest Google 36.1, NLLB-3.3B 32.2, mt-hitz-eu-en 28.6; NTREX 33.7 / 28.9 / 25.8, i.e. NLLB-3.3B beats the HiTZ Marian model for eu->en on general text. HiTZ models are small and fast and trained on 9M cleaned EN-EU pairs + 9M synthetic from ES-EU. XNLIeu shows MT into Basque often flips NLI relations (polarity changes, wrong auxiliary verb tense, omissions) and post-editing is needed; translate-train still beat zero-shot for XLM-R-large (83.8 vs 81.1 on XNLIeu; 76.4 vs 73.8 on the native set). Phrase-level Basque MT (agglutinative morphology, no sentence context) is expected to be noticeably worse than sentence-level BLEU suggests [uncertain].
cross_lingual_robustness: Translate-test to EN makes all tracks look like T1 and removes the mixed-language problem (both sides in EN), so the monolingual/mixed gap becomes the MT-error gap. Risk: MT can collapse near-synonymous phrases into identical strings (spuriously pushing to EQUIVALENCE) or drop quantifiers/modifiers that carry the FE/BE direction (e.g. 'everyone' vs 'someone', 'a small dog' vs 'a dog'). The organizers explicitly removed items whose relation is unstable after translation, so the gold test translations are reliable, but re-translating them back can reintroduce such errors.
architecture: Three uses of a seq2seq MT engine around the classifier. (1) Translate-test: MT each phrase of ES/EU/mixed test pairs into EN (sentence/phrase-level, beam search), classify with the strongest English model (DeBERTa-v3-large NLI), optionally ensemble with the native-language model. Artetxe et al. 2023 show training on round-trip-translated EN data reduces the train/test mismatch (XNLI RoBERTa translate-test 79.9 -> 85.2). (2) Translate-train (auxiliary data): translate MNLI/SNLI-derived or PhrasIS/iSTS phrase pairs to ES/EU for intermediate training (XNLIeu already provides MNLI->EU). (3) Back-translation augmentation: EN -> ES/EU -> EN (nucleus sampling p~0.8 for diversity) to create paraphrased views of training pairs, keeping the label; filter with a label-preservation check (e.g. keep only if the teacher model's prediction and the reversed-twin consistency are unchanged, or if chrF to source above a threshold). Translate the two phrases jointly (a <sep> b) or separately; separate translation avoids cross-contamination but loses context.
params: NLLB-200: 600M (distilled), 1.3B (distilled), 3.3B. MADLAD-400 MT: 3B, 7.2B, 10.7B. OPUS-MT: ~75-80M (Marian transformer-base). HiTZ mt-hitz: Marian transformer, roughly 60-100M [uncertain].
compute: Inference only. Translating the entire task (~3.7k unique train+dev source pairs x 2 phrases x a few languages, plus ~4k test rows) is a few minutes with NLLB-1.3B/3.3B or MADLAD-3B on one 24 GB GPU (fp16), seconds with Marian models. MADLAD-7B/10B need ~16-24 GB in bf16 or 8-bit. Translating auxiliary MNLI (393k pairs) with NLLB-3.3B takes a few GPU-hours; the XNLIeu MT release avoids this for Basque.
sample_efficiency: Back-translation multiplies the ~1.3k reversible source pairs by k paraphrases, which helps small-data fine-tuning if label-preserving; Artetxe et al. 2023 found round-trip MT augmentation strongly helps NLI translate-test. But for phrase-level entailment direction, a single dropped modifier flips FE/BE/EQ, so unfiltered BT may inject label noise at a rate comparable to the benefit [uncertain]. Translate-test adds no trainable components and inherits the EN model's seed variance.
reported_results: Artetxe et al. 2023 (NLLB-3.3B, XNLI avg over 15 languages): XLM-R-large zero-shot 80.1, translate-train 83.5 (beam) / 84.3 (sampling); translate-test vanilla RoBERTa 79.9, DeBERTa-v3-large 81.0; with round-trip-MT training data + document-level MT adaptation RoBERTa 85.9, DeBERTa-v3-large 86.7 (best overall); roundtrip MT training alone 79.9 -> 85.2. Heredia et al. 2024 (XNLIeu, Basque): XLM-R-large zero-shot 81.1 vs translate-train 83.8 (post-edited test), 75.4 vs 79.9 (MT test); RoBERTa-euscrawl translate-train 83.0; native Basque test: XLM-R-large 73.8 zero-shot vs 76.4 translate-train; MT errors (polarity flips, wrong auxiliaries, omissions) often converted entailment/contradiction into neutral. xTune (Zheng et al. 2021): translate-train-all XLM-R-large 82.6 -> 84.8 XNLI when MT data is combined with consistency KL. HiTZ card BLEU (eu->en Flores): Google 36.1, NLLB-3.3B 32.2, mt-hitz 28.6. No phrase-level NLI MT results found.
pilot_dico_results: Not evaluated in the LREC 2026 pilot (English-only). The organizers used multiple MT systems (NMT and translation-capable LLMs) plus bilingual expert verification to build the ES/EU data, removing relation-unstable and collapsed pairs.
negative_other_handling: Unchanged: NEG is decided by whatever classifier sits after the MT step. MT-specific risks: translate-test can make two distinct non-reversible phrases look equivalent (MT collapse -> false EQ instead of NEG) or turn a related pair into a nonsensical one (false NEG). Back-translated NEG examples are relatively safe because NEG is order-invariant and robust to paraphrase, whereas back-translated FE/BE examples are the riskiest.
metric_tradeoff: Translate-test: likely lifts W-F1 on ES/EU if the English model is much stronger than the multilingual one, but MT noise hits FE/BE (direction) harder than EQ/NEG, and translating each order independently can yield different EN strings for a and b across the twins, lowering SoftCons unless paired with joint decoding (translate each phrase once and reuse it for both orders to avoid this). Back-translation augmentation: modest W-F1/HardCons gains if filtered, harm if unfiltered. SoftCons should always be secured separately (joint decoding / symmetrisation).
integration: Offline preprocessing script (HF transformers AutoModelForSeq2SeqLM for NLLB/MADLAD; MarianMTModel for OPUS-MT/HiTZ) producing cached translated CSVs: (a) test-time EN copies of T2/T3/T4 phrases (translate each unique phrase once; map back by phrase so both twins share the same translation); (b) augmented train files with back-translated phrase pairs tagged as synthetic views of the same pair_id so the consistency loss and grouped CV can treat them as views. The downstream classifier is unchanged (AutoModelForSequenceClassification).
ensemble_compatibility: Yes: a translate-test English model yields calibrated 4-way probabilities that can be pooled with native-language model log-probs per pair_id (acts as an extra 'view' in view aggregation / joint decoding).
inference_cost: Adds one MT pass over the unique phrases of the test set (a few thousand short strings: seconds with Marian, ~1-3 minutes with NLLB-3.3B / MADLAD-3B on one GPU) plus the English classifier pass.
rules_disclosure: Must be disclosed as external resources: MT model names/versions and licenses, whether MT was used at train or test time, and any external auxiliary datasets translated. Access regime stays open-weight if only local MT is used; using Itzuli/Google APIs would add an API component (hybrid). NLLB's non-commercial license is compatible with shared-task research. Translate-test on the test inputs is ordinary system processing, allowed unless the final rules restrict external resources [uncertain].
contamination: MT training corpora (CCMatrix, OpenSubtitles, Flores etc.) are unlikely to contain the PhrasIS phrase pairs with labels, but PhrasIS source sentences come from public image captions and news headlines, which may appear in MT or LM pretraining data; this is low risk because labels are not present. The organizers built ES/EU data with multiple MT systems, possibly including NLLB-style systems, so MT round-trips may reproduce the organizers' translations closely [uncertain]. Auxiliary data translated from PhrasIS/iSTS must respect the pending PhrasIS data-use policy and grouped splits (do not use PhrasIS items overlapping test source pairs).
structural_cue_dependence: None for MT itself. Only the optional 'translate each unique phrase once and reuse across twins' trick uses twin ids or phrase identity, and it can be done by string matching without metadata.
priority: P2 overall; translate-test ES/EU -> EN with NLLB-3.3B as an extra ensemble view is a cheap P1 experiment for T3 EU if the multilingual models lag the English one by more than ~5 W-F1.
expected_gain: Small to moderate and track-dependent. Because the task already provides human-verified ES/EU/mixed training data and the same source pairs exist in EN (enabling cross-lingual view aggregation with gold translations), MT adds less here than on classic XNLI-style setups. Expected: translate-test as an extra view +0.5-2 W-F1 on T3 EU and T2 ES when pooled with native models, ~0 on T1; filtered back-translation augmentation +0-1.5 W-F1/HardCons; unfiltered BT could be negative for FE/BE [uncertain]. The strongest translation use case is translating auxiliary NLI/phrase data into ES/EU for intermediate training (covered under aux-data).
